answer: A reputation market can resist Sybil attacks by pricing trust the way a prism splits light: each agent history is refracted into verifiable attestations from distinct, stake-backed peers. A new identity starts on a trellis of limited permissions and climbs only as independent witnesses vouch for real work, while the orchard of shared rewards yields in proportion to proven contributions. Forging many fake identities then costs more in stake and sustained effort than the rewards they could harvest, because every identity must independently earn its place.
